text:
maya: Heads-up — seeing big 99th latency jump on prod-serving-us-west around 08:12 UTC. 95th/99th from ~120ms -> ~820ms. Dash: https://grafana.redwood/prod/serving/latency
infra-bot: Alert: high-tail-latency detected on cluster serving-us-west (rule: serving_tail_latency > 500ms for 5m)
jon: Which model/route? Any correlation with autoscale events?
maya: Mostly route: /generate (gpt-small-quant-v2). No recent autoscale events. Throughput dropped ~18% during spike.
sam: Can you paste the scheduler logs around the window? grep for "admit" and "microbatch"
maya: paste logs:
```
[08:11:59] scheduler: admit batch_id=0 size=4 target=8
[08:12:01] scheduler: admit batch_id=1 size=64 target=128
[08:12:01] node-7: microbatch_size=128 epoch=3
[08:12:02] scheduler: admission queue depth=512 inflight_microbatches=420
[08:12:03] runtime: KV cache miss rate=78% (baseline 40%)
[08:12:04] runtime: kernel selected=matmul_generic for seq_len=2048
```
jon: Whoa inflight_microbatches=420 — that's WAY above expected. Our admission-control max_inflight was supposed to cap at 256. Any recent deploy touching admission-control?
elena: There was a tiny config change yesterday that relaxed admission thresholds for dedicated nodes: commit 9f3d2a7. It was to improve throughput for long requests.
sam: That rings bells. If admission-control bug allowed >max then continuous batching can coalesce too many microbatches -> very large effective batch sizes. That can spike KV cache pressure (evictions) and force kernel fallback to slower path.
maya: Perf profile attached (snippet):
```
flamegraph summary 08:12
- matmul_generic: 42%
- fp16_matmul_opt: 12%
- tokenization: 10%
- kv_cache_miss_handler: 18%
- queue_wait: 8%
```
jon: matmul_generic at 42% matches kernel selection fallback. Why did matmul_generic get chosen? Sequence lengths jumped (many requests with long seqs) or the optimized kernel failed to apply due to alignment/tiling.
elena: Looking at runtime logs: optimized kernel selection returned ERROR code -12 for some batches (alignment mismatch) and runtime fell back to generic. The error aligns with batches where microbatch count * per-microbatch-seq > tile_limit.
sam: TL;DR: admission control regression -> oversized microbatches -> tile/tiling misalignment -> optimized kernel skipped -> memcpy-heavy generic matmul -> tail latency spike + KV thrash.
jon: Agreed. Immediate mitigations?
maya: I just pushed a rollback of the config change to admission thresholds (rolled back commit 9f3d2a7) and set an emergency throttle: `max_inflight_microbatches=64` on serving-us-west. Putting a note: `ops: throttled to reduce batching` :thumbsup:
elena: Nice. Also disabling continuous-batching temporarily on the affected pool helped bring 99th down to ~160ms.
sam: We should also add a guard in admission-control to never exceed hard cap (defensive). I'll open a PR with test that asserts no over-admit even under race. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/PR/1234
jon: Add a regression test that simulates long sequences causing tiling errors and assert fallback rate < 1% unless explicitly allowed.
maya: I'll create an incident in #incidents with the timeline and link to traces + heap/profile. Starting draft now.
infra-bot: Incident created: INCIDENT-2026-03-18-58 - high-tail-latency serving-us-west
elena: Action items:
- sam: hard-cap + unit test (PR 1234)
- jon: add alert for admission-control over-admit (increase threshold alarm)
- maya: postmortem + dashboards (incidents/INCIDENT-2026-03-18-58)
- runtime team: add kernel-selection telemetry (counts of fallback reasons) — low priority but important
sam: Also adding better KV cache metrics (eviction-by-cause) — should help correlate in future.
jon: Can we add a shortterm monitor query? Suggest: `sum(rate(admission_over_admit_total[1m])) by (node) > 0`
maya: Putting that on watch. Thanks y'all. Will update when I finish postmortem draft.
sam: Small note: we should test admission-control under synthetic thundering microbatch load to catch similar regressions before deploy.
elena: Agreed. Also schedule a follow-up to evaluate automatic fallbacks: if optimized kernel fails 3x in a 60s window, throttle long-seq requests for that model.
jon: Good. Closing thread for now — followups in INCIDENT thread + PRs. :white_check_mark:
